question: What is the main purpose of statistical software in research?

options.A: To replace human researchers entirely in the field
options.B: To organize and analyze numerical data quickly
options.C: To automatically write final research manuscripts
options.D: To design colorful hospital posters and flyers

explanation: Statistical software handles complex calculations and data management so researchers can find patterns without manual errors. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T3#BMP314_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why should midwifery researchers avoid doing large data calculations completely by hand?

options.A: Statistical software is the only way to write interview questions
options.B: Manual calculations are slow and invite human error
options.C: Paper records disappear immediately after data collection
options.D: Calculators are illegal to use in modern Nigerian hospitals

explanation: Processing large sets of numeric data manually increases the risk of arithmetic mistakes that computers avoid. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T3#BMP314_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which software option is best known for a menu-driven, point-and-click interface used widely in healthcare research?
explanation: SPSS uses clear menus and dialogue boxes, making it very approachable for healthcare professionals without deep programming backgrounds. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T3#BMP314_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which of the following is a free, open-source programming environment requiring command syntax for data analysis?
explanation: R is a free, open-source programming language relied upon for advanced statistical analysis and custom data graphics. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T3#BMP314_U2_T3_h2)

question: In a standard quantitative data matrix, what does a single row typically represent?

options.A: An individual study participant or record
options.B: An interview question about medical history
options.C: The name of the software package used

explanation: Rows hold individual cases or subjects, while columns hold the specific variables measured for each subject. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T3#BMP314_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why do researchers convert text answers like 'Yes' or 'No' into numbers before entering them into statistical software?

options.A: Ethical boards forbid any text from appearing in spreadsheets
options.B: Patients refuse to answer questions written out as words
options.C: Computers process and analyze numbers much more efficiently
options.D: Numbers take up physical space on paper questionnaires

explanation: Statistical software packages are optimized to perform mathematical and statistical calculations on numeric codes rather than text strings. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T3#BMP314_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of the data cleaning process?

options.A: To physically wash paper questionnaires with soap and water
options.B: To translate research questionnaires into local languages
options.C: To screen the dataset for errors and inconsistent entries
options.D: To delete all participants who disagree with the findings

explanation: Data cleaning identifies mistakes, out-of-range numbers, and missing values so that final analyses are accurate. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T3#BMP314_U2_T3_h4)

question: You notice a patient record in your maternity dataset lists an age of 130 years. What is this an example of?

options.A: An out-of-range error requiring data cleaning
options.B: A normal physiological finding in rural Nigeria
options.D: A perfectly coded categorical variable entry

explanation: An age of 130 is biologically implausible and points to a data entry typo that must be corrected or investigated. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T3#BMP314_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which type of statistics is used to summarize basic sample features like averages and percentages?
explanation: Descriptive statistics organize and summarize raw data features like mean, median, mode, and frequency distribution. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T3#BMP314_U2_T3_h5)

question: When would a midwife researcher use inferential statistical tests?

options.A: To convert text survey answers into numerical computer codes
options.B: To calculate the exact total number of patients seen yesterday
options.C: To clean spelling mistakes out of written interview notes
options.D: To test hypotheses and draw conclusions about a broader population

explanation: Inferential statistics help researchers make inferences or generalizations from a study sample to the wider patient population. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T3#BMP314_U2_T3_h5)

question: What does anonymization involve when preparing healthcare data for software analysis?

options.A: Removing patient names and replacing them with ID numbers
options.B: Translating medical diagnoses into complex foreign languages
options.C: Printing out physical paper copies of every single patient file
options.D: Deleting all numerical variables from the computer spreadsheet

explanation: Anonymization strips away direct identifiers like names to protect participant privacy during and after data processing. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T3#BMP314_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which of the following practices represents an ethical breach in digital health data management?

options.A: Sharing unencrypted patient files over public email or unsecured flash drives
options.B: Storing encrypted datasets on a secure password-protected hospital server
options.C: Removing direct identifiers from survey sheets before computer entry
options.D: Backing up research files onto an institutional cloud storage account

explanation: Using unsecured channels to share identifiable or sensitive health records exposes patients to confidentiality breaches. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T3#BMP314_U2_T3_h6)
